_comment: LINEDOWN — program bill of materials for AI-SRV-G4, assembly level, 480 nodes.
ALL COSTS ARE ILLUSTRATIVE. `unitCostUsd` and `extendedCostUsd` are plausible figures chosen
for the demo, NOT quoted prices. The AGENTS track may replace them with live Tavily data.
Nothing downstream should present any number in this file as fact.
PART NUMBERS are real market part numbers where the component is a real catalogue item.
Lines marked manufacturer 'ODM in-house' use internal part numbers and are illustrative.
SCOPE: top-level assembly BOM, 20 lines. A real program BOM runs to thousands of lines
including passives; this is the level a commodity manager actually works at.
THE ONLY AT-RISK LINE IS BOM-0020 (memory). Two lines are on 'watch' (long lead, still
covered by confirmed POs) to show the desk distinguishes a watch from a line-down.
MODULE vs DIE: BOM-0020 is a complete 288-pin DDR5 RDIMM ASSEMBLY. Sourcing an alternate for
it means buying a different complete module from a different module manufacturer. It never
means substituting DRAM die inside a module.
WHY THE SHORTAGE EXISTS: see BOM-0030. The HBM3 on the GPU baseboards is cannibalising the
conventional DRAM capacity that BOM-0020 is built from. HBM is the cause, not the part being
sourced — there is no module-level alternate for HBM and this desk cannot second-source it.

nodeConfiguration.populationRule: 1DPC, all 24 slots populated, single memory MPN per node — no mixed-vendor population within a node

lines.notes: Sets the memory topology: 12 channels per socket, 24 DIMM slots per node at 1DPC. This is why the memory line is 24 per node and why there is no second DIMM per channel to make up capacity.

lines.plain: This is the broken line. The server needs 24 of these memory sticks each; our supplier will only ship 6,912 of the 11,520 we ordered, leaving 192 of the 480 servers unbuildable.
lines.notes: THE AT-RISK LINE. Allocation cut 40% on 2026-10-03: 11,520 committed, 6,912 confirmed, 4,608 short. Cause is DDR5 wafer starts being reallocated to HBM. Qualified on QVL-G4-2026.08-rev-D, report MV-G4-0244 — the part is fine, the supply is not.

lines.description: HGX H100 8-GPU SXM5 baseboard, 80GB HBM3 per GPU
lines.notes: 3,840 GPUs across the program. The HBM3 on these baseboards is the reason the DDR5 line is short — HBM is cannibalising conventional DRAM capacity. HBM has no module-level alternate and is NOT something this desk can second-source. It is the villain in the backstory, never the sourced part.

lines.description: AI-SRV-G4 mainboard, dual SP5, 24 DIMM, PCIe Gen5
lines.notes: The platform the QVL is written against. Frozen on BIOS G4-BIOS-1.3.2 / AGESA 1.0.0.9b — which is why the 96GB DDR5-5600 SKU (needs 1.4.0) is not a viable fallback.

lines.description: ConnectX-7 400Gb/s OSFP single-port NIC, PCIe Gen5 x16
lines.notes: One NIC per GPU for the compute fabric. Lead time already stretched; second line being watched but not yet at risk.
Storage and management plane offload. Long lead but covered by existing confirmed POs.

lines.description: 7450 PRO 3.84TB U.3 NVMe SSD, PCIe Gen4 x4
lines.notes: Local scratch / dataset staging. Same supplier as the at-risk memory line — worth noting on stage that the allocation cut did not touch NAND.
6 PSUs at 4+2 redundancy for an 8-GPU SXM node.

lines.description: BMC SoC, ASPEED AST2600 rev A3
lines.notes: Reads SPD5 hub and on-module PMIC telemetry — the mechanism by which an unqualified module's thermal behaviour would eventually show up in the field, after the cluster has already shipped.

lines.description: Aries PCIe Gen5 x16 retimer (Smart DSP retimer)

lines.notes: Sets the airflow envelope the QVL thermal soak is validated against: 35C inlet nominal, 70C module case worst case hot-aisle. An unqualified module has no data in this envelope.

rollup.plain: Memory is a small share of what a node costs, but it is 100% of what stops the line. A $214 stick blocks a node worth well over $200,000 — that asymmetry is the whole business case for this desk.

exposure._comment: Illustrative. The burn rate drives the money counter in the UI (alert.raised.burnRatePerMin = 1240).
derivation: idled AI-SRV-G4 final-assembly cell, two shifts — fixed overhead and direct labour
contractual late-delivery penalty accrual on the program
customer-side cluster revenue-at-risk pass-through negotiated into the MSA
exposure.plain: Every minute without a decision costs about $1,240 in idle line time and penalties — roughly $1.79M a day.
